observations.seen: A single directional key with flat ambient fill. The Moon frame is underlit, with a black sky and a muddy gray floor. In the Paris frame the warm light makes the court and the surround the same saturated orange, so the court has almost no figure-ground separation. There is no visible flood rig from the poles.

Players and the net cast crisp, directional shadows, with long shadows in Paris and London. The stands drop hard block shadows. There is no contact darkening or AO where the crowd meets the stands or where the stands meet the floor. Frame 1 shows soft blob-like player shadows that do not match the other frames.

Every surface is matte. There are no specular highlights on the net posts, player gear, or the hard court, and no environment reflection anywhere, including on the Moon court, which should read slightly glossy.

The arena has bleachers, an umpire chair, a bench, two floodlight poles, and a blurred stadium structure behind the far stand. The surround is an untextured ground plane running to the frame edges. The Moon level is a void with a single sphere. The stands are plain boxes.
There is no indoor haze or light shafts. The only depth cue is the blurred backdrop in Paris and London. Frame 1 has a faint green corner glow but no volumetric depth.

Most surfaces are flat vertex color. The frame 1 hard court has a noise or grain texture, and London has mow stripes. The clay, the floor and the bleachers show no roughness variation or surface detail.

The crowd is repeated capsule or blocky figures with no variation in pose. The players are low-poly but readable, with rackets visible. The umpire chair and bench are simple boxes. The net mesh is thin, with a visible kink along its top tape.

In frames 2 to 4 the court is centered and symmetric and fills roughly 30% of the frame, which is within the recipe. A large empty floor wedge fills the bottom of the frame. In frame 1 the court fills about 70%, and the HUD crowds the corners.

This is a perspective broadcast view at about 45 to 50 degrees, not the recipe's orthographic 70-degree view. Frame 1 uses a much steeper, tighter angle than the other three, so the presentation is inconsistent between frames.

There is mild depth of field on the backdrop. The Moon frame has crushed blacks. There is no bloom on the lights or the ball, no color grading per venue beyond the albedo change, and no visible vignette or AA refinement. Thin court lines alias slightly.

Frame 1 has a clean, legible scoreboard, a ball-speed gauge, a power bar, mode pills, and a control strip, but it is dense. Frames 2 to 4 show only an in-world scoreboard text strip. The serve target box is a flat untextured yellow quad that clips across the net.
